# sonrai_account_protected_service (Resource)

Protects one cloud service in one account, firewalling its sensitive permissions for every identity except those exempted here.

A service already protected -- from the console, or by another configuration -- is rejected rather than adopted; import it instead.

Exemptions are attributes of the protect rather than resources of their own: each apply converges the platform's exemption set on the configured one, and the platform removes them when the control is unmanaged or switched to a disable.

The platform's own suggested exemptions are **not** applied. Read them with the `sonrai_suggested_exemptions` data source and list the ones you want, so that the same configuration always produces the same result.

Exemptions granted by a time-limited Permissions on Demand approval are reported in `timeboxed_exempt_identities` and `timeboxed_exempt_sso_actor_ids` and are not managed here: they expire on their own, and listing them would have Terraform fight the approval workflow. A PoD approval granted **permanently** is indistinguishable from one made here, so it is treated as drift and removed on the next apply unless it is added to `exempt_identities`.

Creating this resource *stages* the change. It takes effect only once the pending changes for the containing root scope are submitted and deployed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Protect a service, firewalling its sensitive permissions for every identity
# except those listed. Exemptions belong to the control: removing this resource,
# or switching the service to a disable, removes them too.
resource "sonrai_account_protected_service" "iam_prod" {
  root_scope  = "aws/r-abcd"
  resource_id = "123456789012"
  control_key = "iam"

  exempt_identities = [
    "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CrossAccountIAMAdminRole",
  ]

  exempt_sso_actor_ids = [
    "someone@example.com",
  ]
}

# Protect with no exemptions.
resource "sonrai_account_protected_service" "lambda_prod" {
  root_scope  = "aws/r-abcd"
  resource_id = "123456789012"
  control_key = "lambda"
}

output "iam_prod" {
  value = {
    scope   = sonrai_account_protected_service.iam_prod.scope
    status  = sonrai_account_protected_service.iam_prod.status
    pending = sonrai_account_protected_service.iam_prod.pending
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `control_key` (String) Firewall control key for the service, for example `iam` or `lambda`.
- `resource_id` (String) Cloud-native id of the account to protect the service in: an AWS account id, a GCP project id, or an Azure subscription id.
- `root_scope` (String) Cloud organization root scope, for example `aws/r-abcd`.

### Optional

- `exempt_identities` (Set of String) Cloud-native identities exempt from this control, as ARNs or resource ids, for example `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Admin`.
- `exempt_sso_actor_ids` (Set of String) SSO actor ids exempt from this control. Kept separate from `exempt_identities` because the platform stores and matches them separately.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the form `control_key@root_scope@resource_id`.
- `pending` (Boolean) True while this control has a staged change that has not been submitted and deployed.
- `scope` (String) Canonical scope path this resolved to, recomputed on every read.
- `status` (String) Control status reported by the platform: `Protected`, `Disabled`, `Unprotected` or `Non-Privileged`. Reads `Protected` from the moment a protect is staged.
- `timeboxed_exempt_identities` (Set of String) Identities currently exempt from this control through a time-limited Permissions on Demand grant. Reported for visibility; not managed.
- `timeboxed_exempt_sso_actor_ids` (Set of String) SSO actor ids currently exempt from this control through a time-limited Permissions on Demand grant. Reported for visibility; not managed.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import ID is control_key@root_scope@resource_id.
terraform import sonrai_account_protected_service.iam_prod 'iam@aws/r-abcd@123456789012'
```
